milestones.vision: Stand up the OACP backend (Supabase schema + Edge Functions) and build the TypeScript SDK so that a single agent can register, heartbeat, and be discovered. This is the foundation everything else builds on.
success_criteria: An agent can register via POST /oacp/register and receive a unique agent_id + registry_token
Agent Card (with Ed25519 public key) is persisted in Supabase Postgres
Heartbeat endpoint works and auto-offline detection triggers after 90s silence
Discovery endpoint returns agents filtered by capability tag and status
oacp-sdk TypeScript package exposes register(), heartbeat(), discover() methods
All endpoints validate signatures and return proper error codes
Supabase migration files are version-controlled and reproducible

key_risks.risk: Supabase Edge Functions use Deno runtime — SDK must be isomorphic
key_risks.whyItMatters: If the SDK only works in Node.js, it can't be used in Edge Functions for server-side validation

key_risks.risk: Ed25519 key management in prototype — private keys stored in plaintext config files
key_risks.whyItMatters: Security is a non-goal for v0.1 but must not create patterns that are impossible to harden later

key_risks.risk: Supabase Realtime connection limits on free tier (500 concurrent)
key_risks.whyItMatters: Limits demo scale but acceptable for prototype — must document scaling path

proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: curl/httpie tests against local Supabase show registration, heartbeat, discovery working
A simple agent script using oacp-sdk can register and be discovered
Agent status changes to offline after 90s without heartbeat

milestones.verification_contract: All Edge Function endpoints return correct HTTP status codes and JSON responses. SDK methods are type-safe and match the API contract.
milestones.verification_integration: oacp-sdk can call live Supabase Edge Functions and receive valid responses. Supabase Realtime subscription receives heartbeat status changes.
milestones.verification_operational: Supabase local dev stack (supabase start) runs migrations and serves Edge Functions without errors.
milestones.verification_uat: A developer can run a single agent script that registers, heartbeats, and appears in discovery results.
definition_of_done: Supabase migration files create agents table with all required columns
Edge Functions deployed and responding on /oacp/* routes
oacp-sdk package builds, passes lint, and exports typed API
README documents setup steps and environment variables
All code committed with passing CI checks

milestones.vision: Complete the communication layer: agents can send structured, signed messages to each other through the Supabase message bus, with the SDK providing a clean event-driven API.
success_criteria: Messages table exists with Realtime enabled on recipient_agent_id channel
POST /oacp/messages/send validates envelope schema and verifies sender signature
SDK agent.send(recipientId, payload) composes and signs message envelope
SDK agent.on('task_request', handler) receives messages via Realtime subscription
Two agents in separate processes can exchange a complete task lifecycle

key_risks.risk: Supabase Realtime message ordering is not guaranteed
key_risks.whyItMatters: Task ack/result may arrive before request in race conditions — need sequence numbers
Agent could miss messages during brief disconnects — need catch-up query from messages table

key_risks.risk: Signature verification adds latency to message flow
key_risks.whyItMatters: Must be fast enough for real-time demo feel — Ed25519 verify is ~1ms, acceptable

proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: Messages are stored in DB and delivered via Realtime to correct recipient
Two SDK agents exchange signed messages, verify signatures, and complete a task lifecycle

decisions.decision: Deployment platform for OACP backend API
decisions.choice: Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) for API + Postgres + Realtime; Vercel for web dashboard only; Render for reference agent runtime
decisions.rationale: Supabase provides the full stack needed: Edge Functions for REST API, Postgres for persistence, Realtime for WebSocket pub-sub message bus. Vercel is serverless-only (not suited for persistent agent processes). Render provides persistent Node.js for always-on agent heartbeating. This maps to user's stated deployment preferences.

decisions.decision: iOS app vs web dashboard for demo observer UI
decisions.choice: Build web-based observer dashboard first; defer iOS SwiftUI app to a later milestone
decisions.rationale: iOS app is a significant scope addition (SwiftUI, Supabase Swift SDK, separate build toolchain). A web dashboard achieves the same observer/controller goal with same TypeScript stack, 1/5th the effort. iOS can follow as a separate milestone once the protocol is proven.
decisions.revisable: Yes — can add iOS milestone later

decisions.choice: @noble/ed25519 v3.x for Ed25519 keypair generation, message signing, and verification
decisions.rationale: 5KB, zero dependencies, RFC8032/FIPS-186-5 compliant, SUF-CMA secure, works in Node.js/Deno/browsers. Most widely-used pure-JS Ed25519 implementation (788 dependents). Async and sync APIs available.

decisions.choice: Align OACP Agent Card with A2A Agent Card structure where possible; add protocols_supported field for future A2A bridging
decisions.rationale: A2A is now the dominant agent-to-agent standard (150+ orgs, Linux Foundation governance). Aligning schema structure makes future interop easier. OACP adds registry/relay primitives that A2A lacks, so compatibility is complementary not redundant.
